primary_question: How does canonical SBS-vs-portfolio action-disagreement prevalence change as production-derived workloads move from native replay into progressively resource-constrained serving regimes?

phase_a_native_replay.goal: Support mapping only under native or already-canonical baseline replay.

phase_b_resource_pressure_sweep.goal: Preserve workload identity while varying one serving pressure axis at a time.

axes.notes: Choose and freeze one grid before execution; do not pick after observing support.
Prefer dimensionless fractions of baseline feasible capacity.
Do not fabricate prefix sharing; implement only for traces with genuine prefix/block fields.

phase_c_joint_realistic_regimes.goal: Small predetermined sparse grid over operator-relevant pressure axes.
phase_c_joint_realistic_regimes.rule: Define before execution from Phase-A/B design feasibility, not favorable measured outcomes.

phase_d_causal_headroom.goal: Run expensive one-step SBS-relative counterfactual labeling only after support mapping.
phase_d_causal_headroom.regime_selection_rule: Freeze coverage criteria before labels: native if nonzero support, first-emergence pressure, mid-pressure, high-pressure, and a zero-support control where feasible.
phase_d_causal_headroom.forbidden_rule: Do not choose regimes because they appear to have favorable gains.

phase_e_predictability.goal: Consider learned online prediction only after support/headroom characterization.

anti_cherry_picking: Retain every workload/resource combination in final tables.
Do not make selector accuracy the primary endpoint.
